name: Tfh cell (T follicular helper cell)
summary: A CD4 helper T cell that specialises in helping B cells. It follows CXCL13 to the edge of the follicle and into germinal centres, where it gives B cells that have caught antigen the CD40L and IL-21 signals they need to survive, divide and mature. Without Tfh cells, antibody responses to most protein antigens are weak.
functions: Arises in the T-cell zone from a naive CD4 T cell that a dendritic cell has activated. IL-6 and ICOS signals, and IL-21, push it toward the Tfh state in mice; in humans IL-12 and activin A are important. It switches on the transcription factor BCL6, which raises CXCR5.

Moves to the border of the follicle, guided by CXCL13, where it meets activated B cells showing the same antigen on MHC class II. This first contact decides whether the B cell becomes an early plasma cell or joins a germinal centre.

In the germinal centre light zone it gives B cells CD40L and cytokines (IL-21, IL-4). B cells that show it the most peptide on MHC class II win the most help, which sets how many more times they divide in the dark zone, and so which antibodies win.
Helps choose the antibody class: IL-4 pushes switching to IgE (and to IgG1 in mice), IFN-γ to IgG subclasses that coat microbes well. IL-21 also pushes B cells toward becoming plasma cells.

In humans, cells in blood with CXCR5 (circulating Tfh-like cells) rise about a week after vaccination and can be sampled, but they are resting, memory-like cells, not the Tfh found in germinal centres.
Debated: whether Tfh cells are a separate lineage or a state that any helper T cell can adopt. Their subsets that make IFN-γ, IL-4 or IL-17 resemble Th1, Th2 and Th17 cells.
Debated: how well circulating Tfh-like cells in blood reflect the Tfh in lymph nodes, which are far harder to sample in people.
Shown in mice: a Tfh subset that makes IL-13 and IL-4 drives the IgE antibodies behind severe allergic reactions.
abundance: A minority of CD4 T cells in lymph nodes, higher in tonsils and in lymph nodes making a response. In human blood, roughly 10-20% of CD4 T cells carry CXCR5, but most are resting memory-like cells. Unimmunised laboratory mice have few Tfh cells; they expand in germinal centres after immunisation or infection.
